acceptedPr.title: fix(common): honor DeepSeek Beijing weekend boundaries
acceptedPr.author: c8dhjp4tyv-bit
acceptedPr.body:
> Recreated on the rewritten `main` after #1096 was auto-closed during repository maintenance. This carries the final change set from the old branch onto the new history.

Fixes #1090

## Summary

- Export and directly test the Beijing weekend predicate at the Friday/Sunday UTC boundary.
- Apply DeepSeek's weekend off-peak rule only from its effective instant, 2026-08-22T16:00:00Z.
- Keep historical pricing and expensive-window checks from retroactively treating pre-change weekends as off-peak.

## Why

The existing weekend tests used instants where UTC and Beijing were already on the same weekend day, so removing the `+8` hour conversion left the suite green. The new boundary cases pin Friday 16:00Z and Sunday 16:00Z, where the calendars diverge.

## Verification

Prior validation before the history rewrite:

- `bun test common/src/__tests__/freebuff-peak-hours.test.ts` — 26 passed
- `bun run --cwd common typecheck` — passed
- Prettier check and `git diff --check` — passed

The full `common` test command cannot pass in this public checkout because several existing tests reference private/web files absent from the mirror; the changed test file passes independently.

ai.title: Peak window time zone resolver falls back to UTC on unsupported zones
ai.summary: The weekend/peak-window resolver in `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` now exports `isSupportedTimeZone`, which probes a zone by constructing `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })`, and `resolveWindowTimeZone` uses it so a zone the runtime cannot format resolves to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') instead of throwing. This stops the Cloud model-picker page from crashing in browsers whose `Intl` cannot name a reported time zone, pinning Friday 16:00Z and Sunday 16:00Z boundary behavior.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts`, a new exported `isSupportedTimeZone(timeZone: string)` function was added that constructs `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` and returns false on throw; `resolveWindowTimeZone` was rewritten to use it so an unsupported zone returns `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') instead of throwing. New tests assert fallback-to-UTC, rejection of guarded names, and passthrough of supported zones.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads `isSupportedTimeZone` outside this file or when the fix rolls out to end-user browsers.

eli5.text: The code that decides which AI model you can use for free now checks whether your device's clock can name its own time zone before trying to display one. If it cannot, the message falls back to UTC instead of crashing. This only affects the screen that shows model prices and availability; everyday coding sessions are unchanged, and no action is needed from you.

ai.title: Log data serializer now converts Error objects to structured JSON
ai.summary: `serializeLogData` in `common/src/util/log-data.ts` now detects Error instances during JSON stringification and replaces them with the output of `errorToJson`, which preserves `name`, `message`, `cause`, and a `stack` truncated to `MAX_ERROR_STACK_CHARS = 2_000`. The replacer previously returned Error objects unchanged, so `JSON.stringify(error)` produced `{}` and error rows reached Axiom with no reason attached. facts: Bun's own crash report saying this CPU cannot run the optimized build.
CPU: sse42 avx Features: no_avx2 panic: Illegal instruction at address 0x7FF61902F82C panicked during a panic. Aborting.

Three spellings of one failure, at two levels of certainty. SIGILL STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, or Bun's crash report naming the missing feature (see stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature), is proof this CPU cannot run this build; a Windows startup abort is a strong suspicion (see isStartupCpuFeatureCrash).

Any failed exit, not only a native crash code: a Bun crash on Windows usually exits with plain code 3, and the reason is only in its stderr (see stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature). Clean exits skip the wait.
entries.title: CLI update: launcher

ai.title: Launcher detects Bun AVX2 crash via stderr on Windows code 3
ai.summary:
The Freebuff launcher now reads Bun's stderr tail and matches it against two new constants, BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE (/^Features:[^
]*\bno_avx2\b/m) and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC (/^panic(?:\([^)\n]*\))?: Illegal instruction at address 0x[0-9a-f]+/im), to confirm a missing AVX2 instruction set. Previously the Windows baseline fallback only fired on STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D) or the startup abort 0xC0000409, but a Bun native crash on a pre-AVX2 CPU exits with plain code 3 and the reason is only visible in its stderr. tryFallbackToBaseline() now treats stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature as a confirmed illegal-instruction event and records the machine as lacking AVX2 before downloading the baseline binary, while ordinary exit 3 passes through untouched.
ai.evidence: In cli/release-core/launcher.js, stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature() tests Bun's stderr tail against BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC regexes, and attachExitHandler() now captures stderrTail for any non-zero exit (code !== 0 || signal) instead of only Windows native crash codes, feeding it to tryFallbackToBaseline().
ai.migration: Freebuff, Codebuff, and Codecane users on pre-AVX2 Windows CPUs no longer hit a crash-loop on the optimized build and are automatically moved to the baseline binary on the next launch.
